workarounds.symptom: [BUG]A guardrail that returns a malformed result leaves LLMGuardrailStartedEvent without its completed event

Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/guardrail.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_guardrail_events_on_exception.py. Follow-up to #8403. `process_guardrail` converts the guardrail's return value with `GuardrailResult.from_tuple` after the `try` block that #8403 added, so a guardrail returning the wrong shape (for example `(False, 42)` or a three-item tuple) raised without a `LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent`. The started scope stayed on the event stack: `Agent.... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8648)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] suppress_logging leaves logger levels changed after exit
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(logging): restore configured levels after suppression. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/logger_utils.py, lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_logger_utils.py. Restore the logger's configured level when `suppress_logging()` exits, including after exceptions and interruptions. Previously, a failed ChromaDB query could leave its logger at `ERROR`, hiding subsequent warnings. Successful calls also replaced `NOTSET` with the parent's current effective level, disabling later inheritance. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8215)

workarounds.symptom: EncodingFlow.parallel_analyze crashes the whole save pipeline on transient storage listing failures
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: guard storage listing failures in encoding flow analyze. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/memory/encoding_flow.py, lib/crewai/tests/memory/test_encoding_flow_analyze_fallback.py. `EncodingFlow.parallel_analyze()` calls `storage.list_scopes()` and `storage.list_categories()` unguarded. Both results only feed **suggestion lists** for the LLM field-resolution prompts, yet a transient storage read failure aborts the whole save pipeline: the listener raises, `memory.remember()` re-raises, and the memory is never persisted. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8568)

workarounds.symptom: GuardrailResult result/error exclusivity validator is dead code for the success=True case
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: enforce guardrail result/error exclusivity with model validator. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/guardrail.py, lib/crewai/tests/utilities/test_guardrail_result_exclusivity.py. `GuardrailResult.validate_result_error_exclusivity` is a `@field_validator("result", "error")`, but in pydantic v2 `info.data` only contains **previously validated** fields (declaration order: `success`, `result`, `error`). Validating `result` can never see `error`, so the `success=True` branch of the exclusivity rule is dead code: (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8570)

A `max_usage_count` budget exhausted in an earlier kickoff therefore made **every later kickoff of the same flow object fail**: `B... (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8424)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Crew.test emits CrewTestFailedEvent with no CrewTestStartedEvent when create_llm fails — unpaired scope-ending event pops the caller's scope
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: Crew.test emits its start event before setup so a failed setup pairs. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.test` emits `CrewTestStartedEvent` before `create_llm` (`eval_llm` now carries the requested spec, which the field's `str | Any | None` type already allows) instead of after it, so a setup failure's `CrewTestFailedEvent` has its opener on the scope stack. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8420)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Crew.replay() emits CrewKickoffStartedEvent but no CrewKickoffFailedEvent on failure — leaked kickoff scope corrupts later event lineage
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: replay emits CrewKickoffFailedEvent when the replayed run fails. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/crew.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_crew.py. `Crew.replay`'s execution tail wraps `_execute_tasks` in try/except, emitting `CrewKickoffFailedEvent(started_event_id=self._kickoff_event_id)` before re-raising — mirroring `kickoff()`'s except-clause. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8418)

workarounds.symptom: A guardrail that raises leaves LLMGuardrailStartedEvent without its completed event, so the trace span closes as orphaned
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix: emit LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent when a guardrail raises. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/guardrail.py, lib/crewai/tests/test_guardrail_events_on_exception.py. `process_guardrail` now emits `LLMGuardrailCompletedEvent(success=False, error="<Type>: <msg>")` and re-raises when the guardrail callable raises a non-`HookAborted` exception, mirroring the existing `HookAborted` branch (which keeps its exact legacy error string). (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/8403)

workarounds.symptom: [BUG] Interrupted RWLock acquisition releases a lock it never acquired
workarounds.workaround: Fix: fix(utilities): keep rwlock ownership when acquire is interrupted. Target files: lib/crewai/src/crewai/utilities/rw_lock.py, lib/crewai/tests/utilities/events/test_rw_lock.py. `r_locked()` and `w_locked()` called acquire inside the `try` that always releases in `finally`. If `Condition.wait()` is interrupted before acquire finishes, the context manager releases a lock it never held. The reader count can drop below zero, and the writer flag can be cleared while another writer still owns the lock. (Ref: https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/pull/7944)
